source_refs.note: Topic 12.12.1, printed page 283. The print groups penicillins and cephalosporins with sulfonamides; the lesson keeps the examples and notes the ring sulfur.

blocks.text: Sulfa drugs, the antibacterial sulfonamides, contain sulfur; the print also lists penicillins and cephalosporins, whose ring systems contain sulfur. The common drug omeprazole, used for GERD (gastro-oesophageal reflux disease), contains a sulfoxide group.

blocks.prompt: Identify the sulfur group in omeprazole and name the class of antibacterial drugs built on the -SO2NH- group.
blocks.explanation: Omeprazole contains a sulfoxide, R-S(=O)-R. The antibacterial sulfonamides, the sulfa drugs, are built on the sulfonamide group -SO2NH-.

items: Sulfur in drugs: sulfonamides (sulfa drugs); penicillins and cephalosporins contain sulfur in their rings; omeprazole has a sulfoxide group.
